title: A novel free-air diesel and ozone enrichment research platform
author: Mofikoya, James, et al.

steps.title: Select and prepare site
steps.instruction: Locate the platform at Sonning Farm, University of Reading (51°28′ N, 53°42′ W) on managed grassland with average temperatures 2 °C (Feb) to 22 °C (Jul) and ~709 mm annual precipitation.

steps.title: Build octagonal ring structures
steps.instruction: Construct twelve 8 m‑diameter octagonal rings: drive eight vertical 3 m steel scaffold tubes 40 cm into the ground, spaced 3 m apart; connect each pair with a 3 m horizontal scaffold tube at 1.2 m height; attach eight 15 m flexible corrugated black PVC hoses (25 mm ID, TLC Electrical Supplies, UK) to the horizontal tubes (one hose per tube); on the 3 m hose segment attached to the scaffold, drill 5 mm diameter perforations every 20 cm; seal the hose end on the scaffold with a black plastic cap and connect the opposite end to an eight‑port release manifold.

steps.title: Assign rings to treatment groups
steps.instruction: Designate three rings for each of the four treatments – ambient control (C), ozone (O₃), diesel exhaust (D), and diesel + ozone (D+O₃) – ensuring the centre of any ring is at least 30 m from the centre of any other ring; group rings into four numerical units (1‑4, 5‑8, 9‑12) so each unit contains one ring of each treatment.

steps.title: Install central control container and pumps
steps.instruction: Place a modified 20 ft steel shipping container as the secure central control unit; inside, install twelve R3105 series treatment delivery pumps (Gast, USA) to move ambient air and diesel exhaust through 50 mm ID HDPE conduit to the rings.

steps.title: Configure diesel exhaust conditioning
steps.instruction: Connect a diesel generator (SSDK12W Kubota 12.6 kVA, SGS Engineering Ltd, UK) to the system; route exhaust through a metal conduit for heat dissipation, then through a conditioning volume consisting of three 44‑gallon steel drums (each with a tap for draining) to remove excess water vapour; vent any surplus diesel exhaust away from the site.

steps.title: Mount release manifolds and PVC hoses
steps.instruction: At each ring, install an eight‑port release manifold equipped with Asco series L133 solenoid valves (OEM Automatic, UK); connect manifold outlets to the surrounding 25 mm ID PVC hoses that encircle the ring, ensuring treatment air is released from the upwind sides.

steps.title: Set up air‑diesel mixing valves
steps.instruction: For D and D+O₃ rings, blend ambient air with diesel exhaust using three‑way mixing valves (VRG131 valves and ARA600 proportional actuators, ESBE, Sweden) located in the central control unit to achieve the target NOₓ concentration.

steps.title: Install ozone generators and delivery lines
steps.instruction: Place three CD2000P ozone generators (ClearWater Tech, USA), one per group of four rings; feed each generator with ambient air from a diaphragm compressor (87R637‑101‑N470X, Gast, USA); split each generator’s outlet into two delivery lines, each serving a pair of O₃ and D+O₃ rings, and regulate flow with rotameters for even distribution.

steps.title: Connect ozone tubing to ring manifolds
steps.instruction: Join PTFE ozone delivery tubing to the 50 mm delivery conduit immediately upstream of each release manifold; insert a perforated tube into the conduit to ensure thorough mixing of ozone with the treatment air before it reaches the manifold.

steps.title: Place wind sensors and program release logic
steps.instruction: Install WSD‑V wind speed and direction sensors (Measurement Systems Ltd.) at the centre of each ring; program the control system so treatment air is released from the three upwind sides; if wind speed falls below 0.2 m s⁻¹, open alternate sides on a five‑second cycle to maintain dispersion.

steps.title: Install gas analyzers and sampling manifold
steps.instruction: Mount one Teledyne‑API T400 UV‑absorption O₃ analyzer and one Teledyne‑API T200P photolytic NO₂/NO/NOₓ analyzer (ET enviro, UK) in the central unit; draw filtered air (47 mm PTFE 1.2 µm membranes, Cole‑Parmer, UK) from sampling points at each ring centre through 1/4″ PTFE sample lines to a 12‑port stainless‑steel valve manifold for selection; continuously purge sample lines between measurements.

steps.title: Configure data acquisition and relay controllers
steps.instruction: Set up LabVIEW (National Instruments, TX, USA) control software to start/stop all equipment on a programmable daily cycle; record analogue voltage from wind sensors on USB‑201 DAQ devices (Measurement Computing Corp., MA, USA); switch ring‑side manifold valves via UDP eight‑channel relay controllers (KMTronic, Bulgaria) located at each ring side manifold.

steps.title: Set O3 generator current control
steps.instruction: Provide each ozone generator with a 4–20 mA control signal from a USB‑3104 analogue current output device (Measurement Systems Ltd., UK) to adjust delivered O₃ concentration.

steps.title: Program analyzer timing and start monitoring
steps.instruction: Configure the analyzers (for the period 5 May–7 July 2023) with a purge time of 120 s and a sampling time of 60 s per ring; during each sampling period record pollutant concentrations every second, average them, and automatically save to CSV files; begin the LabVIEW control program to manage wind‑based release, valve operation, and data logging.
